questions.prompt: An `ItemsControl` bound to `Names` shows its items stacked top to bottom. You want them to flow left to right and wrap onto new rows instead. What do you change?
options: Set `ItemTemplate` to a `DataTemplate` whose root element is a `WrapPanel`
Set `ItemsPanel` to an `ItemsPanelTemplate` containing a `WrapPanel`
Set `ItemContainerStyle` with `Margin="8"`
Set `DisplayMemberPath` to the property to wrap
questions.explanation: `ItemsPanelTemplate` decides how items are arranged. By default ItemsControl uses a StackPanel; replacing it with a `WrapPanel` in `ItemsPanel` makes items flow left to right and wrap.

questions.prompt: Your list of projects must let the user select one item. According to the lesson, which control should you use instead of a plain `ItemsControl`?
options: `ListBox`
`StackPanel`
`ContentControl`
`UniformGrid`
questions.explanation: ItemsControl is for displaying data without selection. If you need selection, use a ListBox; if you need columns, use a ListView or DataGrid.

questions.prompt: A teammate writes `<ScrollViewer><ListBox ItemsSource="{Binding Items}" /></ScrollViewer>` for a 50,000-item list, and the UI freezes. Why?
options: ListBox does not support `ItemsSource` bindings when placed inside a ScrollViewer
The ScrollViewer switches the ListBox to `VirtualizationMode="Standard"`
The outer ScrollViewer disables virtualization, so every item gets a container
The ScrollViewer forces `IsVirtualizing` to `True`, which is slower
questions.explanation: Wrapping a ListBox in a ScrollViewer disables virtualization: when the parent measures with infinite size, the VirtualizingStackPanel assumes everything is visible and creates all containers.

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson recommend `VirtualizationMode="Recycling"` over the default `Standard` mode?
options: Recycling creates containers for every item up front, so scrolling never waits
Recycling is the only virtualization mode that works with `ItemsControl`
Recycling turns virtualization off for lists with fixed-height items
It reuses existing containers instead of destroying and recreating them
questions.explanation: Standard mode destroys and recreates containers, while Recycling reuses existing ones, giving minimal GC pressure and the best performance.

questions.prompt: Put the steps a `VirtualizingStackPanel` performs to keep a large list fast in order.
steps: Create containers only for those visible items
Reuse the containers while the user scrolls (when recycling is on)
questions.explanation: The panel measures the viewport, works out which items fit, creates containers only for them, and reuses those containers while scrolling if recycling is enabled.

questions.prompt: A shell window contains `<ContentControl Content="{Binding CurrentView}" />`. How does the app navigate to the dashboard?
options: By opening a new Window for each view
By assigning `CurrentView = new DashboardView();` in the ViewModel
By adding the dashboard to the ContentControl's `Items` collection
By setting `Visibility="Collapsed"` on every other view in code-behind
questions.explanation: A ContentControl holds exactly one piece of content, so the shell swaps views by assigning a new value to the bound `CurrentView`, giving navigation with no code-behind.
